title: Intro to GraphRAG — Zach Blumenfeld
talk_summary: A hands-on Neo4j workshop building a skills/employee knowledge graph with Cypher, entity extraction from resumes, vector+graph hybrid retrieval, and a small LangGraph ReAct agent with four expert tools. It is mostly a GraphRAG tutorial, but a few mechanisms (expert tools over free-form query generation, annotated schema for LLM query generation, materialized similarity edges) transfer to agent orchestration.

takeaways.technique: Expert tools instead of LLM-generated queries for complex traversals
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than letting the model write arbitrary queries, they expose a small set of pre-written functions (retrieve skills of person, find similar skills, person similarity, find people by skills) and let the ReAct agent pick among them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we do often recommend that you have your own expert tools if there's like a really complicated type of traversal that you want to do

takeaways.technique: Annotated schema + example query patterns in the prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: They dump the graph schema as JSON and annotate node labels/properties/relationships with descriptions and canonical query patterns so the model generates correct queries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: putting those actual query patterns into the schema as well helps a lot because the model can read that and then understand how to do that traversal better

takeaways.what_they_do: They precompute a 'similar skill set' edge between people so repeated similarity lookups don't re-run the full multi-hop traversal, accepting staleness and re-running on data updates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we don't have to do that full traversal over and over again if we don't want to um with that similar skill set relationship

takeaways.technique: Hybrid scoring: hard matches + semantic similarity with tunable weights
takeaways.what_they_do: They combine exact overlap counts with vector similarity into a single weighted score, and can adjust weights independently, rather than relying on either alone.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's sort of balancing between the um similar skill set and semantically similar skill set ... we can weight those independently as well

takeaways.technique: Small, natural-language-shaped data models for agent query generation
takeaways.what_they_do: They advise keeping schemas small and naming relationships in plain language so LLM-generated queries are more accurate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: simpler data models seem to work better when you do like dynamic query generation
